rationale: Reviewed the 21 structural lines above against one live swap-api trade page (limit=100) for mainnet mint HgBRWfYxEfvPhtqkaeymCQtHCrKE46qQ43pKe8HCpump, fetched 2026-08-22T01:11:14Z. The document is an object with a trades array beside a pagination object. All 100 rows carried exactly the same fourteen keys with no nulls, which is why the collapsed shape has one $/trades/*:object line. Every value in a trade row is a JSON STRING except nothing: timestamp is an ISO-8601 instant string here, unlike the candle route where timestamp is an epoch-millisecond number, and the price and amount fields are decimal strings retained verbatim and never parsed. MEASURED SEMANTICS THAT THIS SHAPE DOES NOT ITSELF CARRY: rows are descending by slotIndexId, newest first, and slotIndexId was strictly monotone across the page; pagination.nextCursor is the exclusive keyset slotIndexId-epochMillis of the LAST returned row, so a page boundary is reconstructible rather than an opaque server token; feeding it back returned a strictly older page that shared no slotIndexId and no tx with the first, so consecutive pages neither overlap nor skip at the boundary; priceUsd is the pool price the trade printed at and fillPriceUsd is what the taker actually paid, and the signed gap between them was +24.6 basis points on buys and -24.5 on sells across 200 rows, which is the venue fee, not size impact. KNOWN NARROWNESS, accepted deliberately: this fingerprint was observed only on a page with hasMore true and a string nextCursor. A terminal page that presents a null or absent nextCursor has NOT been observed and would produce a different fingerprint and be refused until separately reviewed; that refusal is the intended behaviour of this gate, and nothing here should be read as a claim that the terminal shape is known. This review was made by an agent, not by Ember. It authorises retaining and normalizing provider-asserted trade rows as provider assertions only; it certifies no fill, no execution, and no on-chain fact.
